title: Node Signatures & Health Index — Inventory + Discovery Architecture Notes
content:
Purpose
This doc captures a lightweight, practical model for the cluster inventory (node signatures), service discovery surface, and the health-index used by routing policies across regions. Goal: provide a single, extensible node representation plus a health scoring function that the control plane and router can rely on for fast selection and graceful degradation.

Context and constraints
- We operate multi-region fleets with region-local pools and occasional cross-region failover.
- Inventory must be readable by the control plane router, autoscaler, placement service, and SRE tools.
- Most lookups need to be low-latency; eventual consistency is acceptable for non-critical metrics but routing needs fresh heartbeats and critical health flags.
- We'll prefer label selectors and a small, computed health score rather than complex per-request policy evaluation.

High-level model: Node Signature (flat inventory row)
Each node publishes a compact signature that becomes the canonical inventory row. The signature is the unit of discovery and routing. Example fields (string-typed schema here for Drive doc):
- node_id: <uuid>
- hostname: <string>
- region: <string> (e.g., us-west-2)
- az: <string> (optional)
- pool: <string> (e.g., dedicated-gpu-small)
- labels: comma-separated k=v pairs (see label schema below)
- gpu_types: comma-separated normalized gpu tokens (see gpu mapping)
- gpu_count: integer-as-string
- free_gpu_mem_mb: integer-as-string (best-effort)
- estimated_tokens_per_sec: integer-as-string (sampled running avg)
- last_heartbeat: RFC3339 timestamp string
- health_flags: comma-separated short flags (e.g., HEARTBEAT_MISS, GPU_PANIC, DRIVER_MISMATCH)
- health_score: float-as-string between 0.0 and 1.0 (computed locally)
content_addendum:
Label schema (recommended keys)
We want predictable selectors, so limit label keys and value vocab. Use kebab-case. Sample keys:
- role: inference | batch | training (role describes primary workload)
- tier: prod | canary | test
- instance-class: gpu-xlarge | gpu-medium | cpu-small
- gpu-fam: a100 | h100 | t4 | rtx6000
- memory-tier: high | standard
- locality: zone-level or rack id (optional)
- residency: pii | public | private (helps data residency routing)

GPU type normalization (why)
Cloud providers and on-prem vendors have many descriptors. Normalize to short tokens for selectors and routing logic. Mapping examples:
- nvidia-a100-80gb -> a100-80
- nvidia-h100-80gb -> h100-80
- nvidia-a10 -> a10
- rtx-6000 -> rtx6000
Store these as comma-separated strings under gpu_types and repeated in labels via gpu-fam.

Health signals (what to publish)
We separate signals into three buckets: critical, advisory, telemetry.
- Critical (affects routing immediately): heartbeat_miss, nvlink_error, gpu_panic, out_of_memory, kernel_oops, container_runtime_dead.
- Advisory (influences health_score): high_gpu_mem_pressure (>=85%), high_gpu_temp (>=85C), driver_warn, degraded_nvlink_throughput.
- Telemetry (for monitoring and capacity planning): avg_gpu_util_pct, avg_gpu_mem_pct, cpu_load_1m, disk_io_wait, last_reboot_age_hours.

Heartbeat semantics
- Node heartbeat frequency: 30s default. Heartbeat carries a tiny signature and delta metrics.
- Heartbeat TTL: if last_heartbeat older than 90s -> mark HEARTBEAT_MISS (critical).
- For routing, treat HEARTBEAT_MISS as non-viable; for autoscaler, treat as candidate for drain/eviction.

Local health_score computation (sample algorithm)
Compute a 0-1 score every heartbeat on-node. Score is a weighted product of critical pass/fail and scaled advisory penalties:
- If any critical flag set => health_score = 0.0
- Base = 1.0; apply multipliers: free_gpu_mem_ratio -> score *= clamp(free_mem_mb / total_mem_mb, 0.0, 1.0) ^ 0.5; temp_penalty = clamp((85 - (85 - temp_c)) / 85, 0, 1) applied as a 0.9 multiplier if over threshold; gpu_util_penalty reduces score linearly if sustained > 95% for X mins.
- Round to 2 decimals and publish.
This keeps evaluation cheap and deterministic. The router uses health_score threshold (e.g., >=0.6) and stable health_score_history for decisions.

Discovery API surface (read-oriented)
Control plane exposes region-local read endpoints with simple filtering:
- GET /inventory/v1/nodes?label=role:inference&gpu_fam=h100&min_health=0.7&pool=dedicated-gpu-small&limit=50
- GET /inventory/v1/nodes/{node_id} (single row)
- POST /inventory/v1/query (lightweight selector language for async jobs)
Responses are paginated lists of Node Signatures. Writes (heartbeats) are pushed by node agents to an ingest endpoint and mirrored to regional stores.

Consistency model and reconciliation
- Write path: node-agent -> region-ingest -> local regional store (fast path). The region store is authoritative for that region.
- Cross-region replication: async, periodic (every 30s–2m) with conflict-free last-write-wins per field and TTL-based eviction for stale rows.
- Reconciliation: a control-plane sweep job performs a full inventory sync across regions every 10 minutes to detect split-brain or long-stale entries and to repair mismatched labels or driver versions (tag drift).
- Rationale: fast regional reads, low-latency routing. Cross-region eventual consistency is acceptable for non-failure traffic; explicit failover uses health checks and last_heartbeat freshness.

Routing policy integration
Router picks nodes using: label selectors -> candidate list -> sort by composite score -> apply capacity gating. Composite score = alpha*health_score + beta*latency_penalty + gamma*recent_error_rate_adjustment + delta*cost_penalty. Tunable weights per product tier (prod vs canary).
Fallbacks: if no nodes match strict selector, progressively relax label constraints (e.g., allow tier=test then region=adjacent) with an explicit cost/latency surcharge and audit log.

Multi-region considerations
- Region-stickiness: requests default to same region pool if candidates available above min_health.
- Cross-region routing only allowed for specific routes/models with explicit policy and consent (billing/residency).
- Control plane must tag nodes with residency and compliance labels to prevent accidental cross-region serving of sensitive workloads.
- Cold-start for capacity: autoscaler signals via inventory (desired_capacity label) and placement service reserves warm nodes tagged warm=true.

Operational concerns
- Label drift: add an enforcement job that verifies labels on node against expected instance metadata at start-of-day; reconcile or flag.
- Driver/runtime mismatches: mark as DRIVER_MISMATCH advisory flag; escalate to SRE if persists > 15m.
- Metric cardinality: store only aggregated telemetry in inventory row (moving detailed metrics to TSDB) to keep inventory queries cheap.

Data model examples (text form)
node_id: 8b2f4c78-...
hostname: infer-uw2-1234
region: us-west-2
az: us-west-2b
pool: dedicated-gpu-small
labels: role=inference,tier=prod,instance-class=gpu-xlarge,gpu-fam=h100,residency=public
gpu_types: h100-80
gpu_count: 4
free_gpu_mem_mb: 51200
estimated_tokens_per_sec: 92000
last_heartbeat: 2024-10-03T18:12:08Z
health_flags: 
health_score: 0.92

Migration plan (phased)
1) Pilot: select one regional fleet, deploy node-agent that publishes new signature + health_score. Router reads both old inventory and new signatures in parallel for 2 weeks.
2) Soft enforce: switch a subset of traffic (10-20%) to use new selectors and health_score gating. Monitor latency and p50/p99 errors.
3) Cutover: once stable, switch router to authoritative new inventory. Turn on cross-region replication for other regions.
4) Clean up legacy fields and remove dual-read path.

Open questions / trade-offs
- Should we accept per-request on-router health probes (extra latency) or rely purely on heartbeat/score? Recommendation: avoid per-request probes; keep probes for long-lived connection validation only.
- How much cardinality do we accept in labels (rack, GPU binning)? Keep labels limited to 10 keys to avoid explosion.
- Eviction semantics for intermittent HEARTBEAT_MISS: immediate remove vs mark drained. We favor mark drained (non-viable for new allocations) then eviction after 5 minutes if not recovered.

Action items
- [Samir] finalise health_score formula and publish a reference implementation in infra-agent (PR: linked above).
- [Lina] build router integration stub to read min_health filter and composite scoring hooks.
- [Marcus] implement reconciliation sweep job scaffold and smoke tests for label drift.
- [Priya] write runbook for DRIVER_MISMATCH and HEARTBEAT_MISS escalations.

References
- Regional routing controls (Confluence)
- ENGPLAT-4823 (inventory v2 epic)
- infra PR #734 (agent heartbeat schema draft)

Notes: This is an intentionally pragmatic design: keep the inventory row small, compute health on-node, and rely on label selectors plus a single health_score to make routing decisions fast and auditable. We can iterate on the score formula as we collect production telemetry.
